display.title: The Flax Merchant: Rabbi Zusha, Shivisi and Hashgachah Pratis
display.summary_short: A class on Rabbi Zusha's letter shin of teshuvah, a story of the Alter Rebbe's new script, and the flax merchant who freed fellow Jews and was blessed with two tzaddikim for sons.
display.summary_long: Linking the day's Hayom Yom to a song the children just sang, the storyteller explains Rabbi Zusha of Anipoli's teaching on the five letters of teshuvah: shin stands for 'Shivisi Hashem l'negdi samid', Hashem is always with me and every step is planned. He shows Rabbi Zusha's holiness with a story: when the Alter Rebbe, at the Maggid's request, designed a new script for tefillin, mezuzos and sifrei Torah, he visited the scribe Rabbi Moshe Sofer and found him already writing tefillin in the new script for Rabbi Zusha, who knew of it through ruach hakodesh. Then a story of hashgachah pratis: Reb Eliezer Lipa, a rich flax merchant who loved freeing Jews from the poritzim's dungeons, dozes on the road and his horse leads him to a stranded poritz. He overhears the poritz threatening a Jewish innkeeper, later pays the innkeeper's whole debt with his deposit money, and refuses to deal with another poritz until a Jewish boy held hostage is sent home. In Heaven it is decided that such a man deserves two special sons: Rabbi Zusha and Rabbi Elimelech.
display.lesson: Hashem is always with us and guides every step, and going out of your way to help another Jew brings great blessing.
